Only `referenceFamily_length` and `referenceFamily_actualX` are tagged `@[simp]`. There are no simp lemmas for `width`, `rowSlope`, `originX`, `originZ` or `site`. I read the definitions of `snappedSite`, `positiveEnvelope`, `absoluteConstant`, `physicalFrozenCenteredCoefficient`, `physicalMainScale`, `physicalMainSquare` and `physicalCenteredMaskedBand`. I also read `sum_reference_frozen`, the sibling file SourceReferencePhysicalIdentity.lean, and the downstream uses in SourceLabeledNarrowTail.lean, SourceLabeledActiveReference.lean and SourceSelectorConcentrationActive.lean.

The narrow-restriction equalities (`*_eq_narrow_reference`) need hypotheses and rewrite P to Q. They are correctly left untagged. `physicalFrozenCenteredCoefficient_eq_zero` is conditional on a hypothesis about all k, so it is not a good simp lemma either.

What remains uncertain: I could not run Lean. The proposed simp-based proofs are untested, and they rely on the subterms matching up to reducible defeq. If simp's final `rfl` check fails, a trailing `rfl` may still be needed. The `@[simp]` proposal for `referenceSelf_frozenCenteredCoefficient` is weaker than the others. Its left side contains the lambda `fun j l k s => b j (orig j l) k s`, which may not match well as a simp pattern. For that reason I suggest passing it explicitly to `simp only` rather than tagging it.

findings.problem: The expression `(Q).snappedSite j l u` unfolds to `snappedLatticeSite ((Q).originX j l) ((Q).originZ j l) ((Q).length j) (Q).width ((Q).rowSlope j l) ((Q).site j l u)`. Simp has no rules for the `referenceFamily` projections `originX`, `originZ`, `rowSlope`, `site` and `width`. Only `length` and `actualX` have `@[simp]` lemmas. As a result, the proof has to restate the entire unfolded `snappedLatticeSite` application with `change` before the `(t-t)` terms can be cleaned up. The same gap forces a long `change` in `referenceFamily_physicalPacket`. The desired normal form is that each projection of `referenceFamily old new …` is written in terms of `P` at `orig j l`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add rfl-proved `@[simp]` projection lemmas next to `referenceFamily_length` in SourceReferenceRestriction.lean, stated in the same style:
- `referenceFamily_width : (P.referenceFamily …).width = P.width`
- `referenceFamily_originX … = P.originX j (P.referenceOriginalLabel … j l)`
- `referenceFamily_originZ … = P.originZ j (orig j l) + (oldSlope-newSlope)*P.originX j (orig j l)`
- `referenceFamily_rowSlope … = P.rowSlope j (orig j l) + (oldSlope-newSlope)`
- `referenceFamily_site … = P.site j (orig j l)`

Then the proof here becomes `simp [snappedSite]`. Simp unfolds both sides, rewrites the projections, and turns `(t-t)` into `0` with `sub_self`, `zero_mul` and `add_zero`. The rewrites only move from Q-projections to P-terms, so there is no cycle.
findings.benefit: The proof no longer duplicates the body of `snappedLatticeSite`, which is fragile if the argument order or definition changes. The same simp lemmas would also shorten `referenceFamily_physicalPacket` and the `(t-t)` cleanup anywhere `referenceFamily t t` is used.

findings.problem: `referenceSelf_absoluteConstant` (line 41), `referenceSelf_snappedSite`, `referenceSelf_positiveEnvelope` and `referenceSelf_alt_physicalPacket` all rewrite a projection of the reference family `Q` to the matching `P` quantity at `orig j l`. None of them needs a hypothesis. That is the natural canonical direction, and it is the same direction as the existing `@[simp] referenceFamily_length` and `referenceFamily_actualX`. None of them is tagged `@[simp]`, and `referenceSelf_absoluteConstant` is not used anywhere. Because the rules are not usable by simp, both narrow-restriction proofs (lines 102-108 and 167-173) open the double sum by hand with nested `Finset.sum_congr rfl` / `intro` and then `rw`. Each rule is written out with all 11 explicit arguments `t R cone w F hw hcone hF hwide hfrequency`.
findings.proposed_change:
Tag `referenceSelf_absoluteConstant`, `referenceSelf_snappedSite`, `referenceSelf_positiveEnvelope` and `referenceSelf_alt_physicalPacket` as `@[simp]`. Each right-hand side mentions only `P`, so these rules cannot cycle with each other or with the existing `referenceFamily_*` simp lemmas. Then replace each five-line `sum_congr` block with one call:
- for the main scale: `simp only [P.referenceSelf_frozenCenteredCoefficient t R cone w F hw hcone hF hwide hfrequency, referenceSelf_positiveEnvelope]`
- for the masked band: the same, with `referenceSelf_alt_physicalPacket` in place of `referenceSelf_positiveEnvelope`

Simp rewrites under the `∑` binders by itself. I would keep the frozen-coefficient lemma as an explicit simp argument rather than a global `@[simp]`, because its left side contains the lambda `fun j l k s => b j (orig j l) k s`.
findings.benefit: Downstream proofs about `referenceFamily t t …` could normalize reference-family envelopes, packets and constants with `simp` instead of hand-written congruence steps and 11-argument rewrites. The currently unused `rfl` lemma `referenceSelf_absoluteConstant` would also become useful, for example when simplifying `(Q).constant`-style expressions.
